title: [V1][Spec Decode] Optimize N-gram matching with Numba (#13365)

experiments.name: ngram_match_overhead
experiments.workload: 5000 synthetic context sequences (len 200-800, vocab 32000), n-gram n=3, k=10; ~50% seeded with a plantable match. Cumulative NgramProposer.propose() time over the full 5000-seq pass; 5 repeats (gold warmed up once untimed to exclude JIT compile).
experiments.note: PREFERRED approach: imported the standalone vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py module directly from each mounted source tree (self-contained, only numpy/numba/typing deps) and timed .propose(). base=pure-python KMP loop; gold=numba @jit(nopython=True) kernels. runs = per-repeat cumulative seconds; speedup_x = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios. numba not baked in image -> installed at runtime via pip (numba 0.68.1, arm64 wheel); worked.

reported.scope: cumulative over a full ShareGPT 5K-request E2E serving run (propose() called once per decode step per request = hundreds of thousands of calls)
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (s) but NOT scale-comparable to our microbench. Our 'base' 0.257s is cumulative over 5000 single-sequence propose() calls; the PR's 54.3s is cumulative over a full ShareGPT 5K-REQUEST serving run (~200x more cumulative work; exact call count not derivable since per-call cost differs between synthetic and real token streams). Direction + ratio (ours 71x vs reported ~29x) are genuine; absolute seconds are not 1:1.

environment: docker vllm-cpu-bench:21222 (python:3.12-slim + CPU torch arm64 wheel, numpy 2.5.4), colima arm64 Mac; identical image for both arms, only vllm/ source tree differs. numba NOT baked into image -> installed at runtime with `pip install numba` (numba 0.68.1, arm64 wheel) for the gold arm; base arm is pure-python and needs no numba. gold arm warmed up once (untimed) to exclude numba JIT compile from the steady-state timing.
